The video then touches on 4 major points:

The first point is that single celled organisms are too complex to have come about randomly. Charles Darwin and his contemporary scientists did not know that DNA existed and thought that things got simpler as they got smaller towards the molecular or quantum levels. Francis Crick, co-discoverer of DNA, calculated that the odds of a single protein assembling all the amino acids in the right specific order by accident would be 1 in 10^260 - a number higher than the amount of electrons you could fit into the known universe. Mathematicians would tell you that any odds higher than 1 in 10^50 is essentially impossible. A single cell consists of thousands of proteins. A single cell thus needs thousands of proteins assembling in the right order each at effectively impossible odds.

The second point the clip talks about is DNA. Darwinian scientists initially rejected and resisted the concept of DNA when it was first discovered because Darwinism now had to explain away this phenomena as well. As DNA science illustrates, you cannot pass off new genetic information to your offspring. Offspring can only contain the same genetic information as the parents. The only way to bypass this is to suggest new DNA information is introduced through random mutations. The problem with this is that all observed random mutations have always lead to a degradation in genetic information, not an increase, and all observed mutations have lead to a lessened likelihood of survival.

The third point is the fossil record. There ought to be billions of fossils of transitional species and for dead-end mutations as well. There are none. The fossil record as it stands so far shows animals that all fit together in exact specific categories (ie. microorganisms, invertebrates, fish, mammals, etc.) with no in-between creatures. Many of the supposed missing links found have later turned out to be hoaxes or even animals that are still alive today.

The last point touched on is irreducible complexity (ie. a body consists of several highly complex parts that are interdependent). If you take away one component of one of these parts then the entire body fails to function. Darwinian evolution would need for complex, multi-part, interdependent functions to have sprung about randomly all at the exact same time and not in stages.
